newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends weaker, upside seen limited.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends weaker, upside seen limited.

text.p: CSCE world sugar prices ended lower Thursday, hit by speculative and arbitrage selling as well as price fixing by producers at the highs, trading sources said.

The market drifted in negative territory throughout the entire day, slowly working its way lower as operators took profits on the raws' recent run-up. Producers were keen sellers toward 10.65 cents a lb, while scale-down buying by processors provided support near 10.60 cents.
Arbitrage selling against the London market also figured in New York's weakness today, spurred the recent steep decline on the whites' March/March premium, dealers said.

Benchmark New York March closed down 0.09 at 10.59 after trading from 10.57 to 10.68. Second-position May fell 0.05 cent to 10.65, while the outer months eased 0.04. An estimated 9,014 lots changed hands on the day.

With little physical offtake to buoy the market, traders said raws could be gearing up for a test of recent lows. Today's high of 10.68 cents matched Wednesday's peak, creating a bearish double top on the charts, they pointed out.

"The market is starting to give the impresssion that the consolidation may be over," said one trader. "If we can't get back to Tuesday's high of 10.71 cents, it's going to work it's way back down again."
March sugar would need to hold above the crucial 10.50-cent mark or risk facing a heavy bout of stop-loss selling, he said.
